security_audit.summary: The audit confirms that this skill intentionally guides Claude Code to run Codex CLI, including workspace-write, full-auto, danger-full-access, session resume, and stderr suppression patterns. Installation paths and most Markdown backtick detections are documentation false positives, but the operational instructions can still create shell-injection, hidden-warning, and broad-access risks if used without explicit approval. No evidence found of prompt injection language, secret exfiltration, or hidden malware behavior in README.md or SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Shell prompt construction for session resume
remediation.suggestion: Avoid echo-piping raw user prompts through a shell. Pass prompt text through safe stdin handling or document strict quoting requirements.
Require explicit user approval before full-auto, danger-full-access, or skip-git-repo-check. Prefer read-only mode for reviews.
Show stderr for failed, security-sensitive, or warning-producing runs. Summarize diagnostics instead of discarding them by default.
Use a unique temporary directory and cleanup trap instead of a fixed rm -rf path in installation examples.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Prompt Piping Can Alter Commands
semantic_findings.description: The resume workflow pipes prompt text through echo into codex exec. If an assistant inserts unescaped user text into that shell command, metacharacters can change execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The shell pipeline examples are explicit, but the files do not include an executable wrapper. The risk depends on how user prompt text is quoted at runtime.

semantic_findings.title: Default Stderr Suppression Reduces Auditability
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends suppressing Codex stderr by default. This can hide warnings, policy messages, or error details during automated command execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The redirection is repeated in both the README and skill instructions. The stated goal is context control, but hidden diagnostics are a real reviewability concern.

semantic_findings.title: Repository Check Bypass Is Required By Default
semantic_findings.description: The skill says to always use the skip-git-repo-check flag. This bypasses a safety check that can help limit Codex runs to expected repository contexts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit and repeated in operational examples. The file also requires permission for high-impact flags, which reduces but does not remove the risk.

content.user_title: Run Codex CLI from Claude Code
content.value_statement: Claude Code users need a structured way to delegate code analysis and edits to Codex. This skill defines Codex CLI commands, sandbox choices, resume flows, and review summaries.
actual_capabilities: Guides Claude Code through Codex CLI task setup.
Documents model, reasoning effort, sandbox, and directory options.
Supports read-only review, local edits, broad-access tasks, and session resume.
Explains when Codex stderr is suppressed or shown.
Requires user approval before high-impact flags.
Summarizes Codex results and asks for follow-up direction.
limitations: Requires Codex CLI to be installed and authenticated first.
Can be risky when full-auto or danger-full-access modes are approved.
May hide useful diagnostics when stderr is redirected to null.
Model names, prices, and version guidance may become outdated.

use_cases.title: Review a repository with Codex
use_cases.description: Run a read-only Codex analysis and summarize architecture, testing, and maintainability issues.

use_cases.title: Delegate focused refactoring work
use_cases.description: Use Codex to plan and apply approved local edits with an explicit sandbox mode.

use_cases.title: Continue a prior Codex session
use_cases.description: Resume the latest Codex session and provide a follow-up request through standard input.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze This Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Codex to review this repository in read-only mode. Summarize the most important bugs, risks, and test gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Codex to inspect the current module and propose a small refactor plan. Do not edit files until I approve the plan.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Approved Edits
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Codex with workspace-write access to implement the approved change. Report files changed, tests run, and any failures.

prompt_templates.title: Resume and Deepen Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume the last Codex session and focus on security, failure modes, and missing regression tests.

output_examples.input: Use Codex to analyze this repository for maintainability issues.
output_examples.output: A concise review summary with prioritized findings, affected areas, and recommended next steps.

output_examples.input: Use Codex to implement the approved refactor.
output_examples.output: A change report listing modified files, verification results, and any follow-up work.

output_examples.input: Resume the last Codex session and continue the security review.
output_examples.output: A continuation summary that preserves prior context and focuses on unresolved security concerns.

best_practices: Use read-only mode for review tasks unless edits are required.
Approve full-auto or danger-full-access only for trusted repositories and clear tasks.
Request stderr output when debugging failures or reviewing security-sensitive runs.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad access modes on untrusted repositories.
Do not paste sensitive secrets into Codex prompts.
Do not treat suppressed stderr as proof that a command succeeded cleanly.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It tells Claude Code how to run Codex CLI for code review, refactoring, editing, and session continuation.

faq.question: Does it require Codex CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex CLI must be installed, available on the PATH, and configured with valid credentials.

faq.question: Can it edit my files?
faq.answer: Yes, if you approve workspace-write or broader access. Use read-only mode for analysis-only work.

faq.question: Why does it suppress stderr?
faq.answer: The skill suppresses stderr to reduce context usage. Ask to show stderr when debugging or auditing a run.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use only read-only mode for untrusted repositories. Avoid full-auto and danger-full-access in those cases.

faq.question: Can it resume a Codex session?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes guidance for resuming the latest Codex session with a follow-up prompt.
